The search turned up several GitHub threads on this. Most trace the mismatch to extensions that change the DOM before React hydrates, and the usual fixes are disabling the extension or suppressing the warning.

- **ColorZilla is the most-reported case.** In Next.js issues #72031 and #72035, the ColorZilla extension adds a `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute, and when Colorzilla is disabled, the hydration error resolves. A maintainer said these hydration errors come from React and not Next.js. Another commenter suggested tweaking the settings to only allow CZ to modify the page when you actually click the extension. One user shared a workaround that injected a small client-side script that removes the attribute before hydration and uses a MutationObserver to prevent it from being re-added.
- **React's stated position.** Per the Video Speed Controller issue (#1255), React's view is that extensions should mostly avoid generating unexpected HTML, and React 19 skips unexpected tags in head and body, which avoids mismatch errors. That issue also covers an extension that adds a class to the html element and triggers the error.
- **Open React bug.** Issue #36169 (React 19.2.4) reports that a `<script defer>` inside `<head>` triggers hydration errors even without extensions, and the docs note that an extension installed on the client can change the HTML before React loads.
- **Workarounds in PRs.** Several pull requests add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the root `html` or `body` element. One notes that suppressHydrationWarning applies only to the element's own attributes, never to its children, so a real mismatch anywhere inside the tree is still reported. These are proposed fixes in individual repos, not an upstream React change.
- **Suppressing the error is hard.** A Sentry issue (#15886) reports that Sentry does not seem to ignore the error when a user tried to filter out the React 418 hydration message.

One caveat: the React-side issue #25924 is from the React 18.2 era, so it predates React 19. The Next.js and PR threads are the closest match to React 19 specifically.

content.text:
Yes. There are several known threads, though none is a single canonical React 19 issue.

- **ColorZilla and Next.js 15 with React 19:** the extension injects a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute into the page, which causes the hydration error. Disabling the extension fixes it. A maintainer said the error comes from React, not Next.js. Links: [issue #72031](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/72031) and [discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035).
- **React issue on extension-injected scripts:** [facebook/react#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924) covers scripts injected by browser extensions, such as React DevTools, causing hydration errors. It was filed in the React 18.2 era, so it predates React 19.
- **Video Speed Controller extension:** [igrigorik/videospeed#1255](https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255) reports a hydration error in the Next.js dev server. It also records React's position that extensions should avoid injecting unexpected HTML. React 19 skips unexpected tags in `<head>` and `<body>`, but an extension that changes attributes or classes on `<html>` still triggers the error.
- **Sentry:** [getsentry/sentry-javascript#15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886) is about ignoring the React 19 hydration error in Sentry.

The usual workaround is `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` or `<body>`. It only covers that element's own attributes, so a real mismatch deeper in the tree is still reported.

Sources:
- [vercel/next.js#72031](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/72031)
- [vercel/next.js discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035)
- [facebook/react#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924)
- [igrigorik/videospeed#1255](https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255)
- [getsentry/sentry-javascript#15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886)
